title: BOS-724 — a dropped --host ssh tunnel names why it went down instead of going silent, and still recovers to the session board unaided

env.BOSS_HOST_E2E_RECONNECT_REASON: remotehost: ssh tunnel to user@build-box exited: signal: terminated

scenes.title: The reconnecting screen reports the supervisor's own diagnosis, so the user learns why the tunnel dropped without reading source

waitFor.label: the screen names the ssh destination it is redialling rather than leaving a --host session looking frozen

steps.caption: The forwarded socket stopped answering; boss shows the reconnecting screen instead of a dial error against a local temp path.

expect.label: the retained classification is labelled on screen — before BOS-724 it only ever reached a Debug line the user could not read
the reason itself is the supervisor's classified exit, which is what makes the next occurrence diagnosable in one step

expect.text: Boss keeps redialling and resumes automatically
expect.label: the screen still promises unaided recovery — the diagnosis is added to the affordance, not substituted for it
the retained action bar keeps a way out, so a reason line never costs the user their escape hatch

steps.caption: Destination, the retained failure reason, the automatic-retry promise, and the escape hatch are all on one frame.

scenes.title: When the tunnel answers again the TUI proceeds to the remote daemon's session board with no keystroke

waitFor.label: the session board replaces the wait screen on its own — reporting a reason did not turn a recoverable outage into a dead end

steps.caption: The redial succeeded; boss resumes startup against the recovered tunnel rather than making the user relaunch.
The wait screen releases the alt-screen and Home completes its first session refresh against the recovered client.

expect.label: a real session row from the daemon renders, so the recovered client is genuinely serving data

steps.caption: The board is populated: the reconnecting screen handed over to a working client.
